classification.difficultyReason: Combine unscaled component graphs while preserving endpoints, asymptotes, cancellation and changes in shape.

spec.description: An increasing exponential-shaped blue curve and a decreasing red straight line meet on the positive y-axis. Both continue outward.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled input curves; add their ordinates. No ticks, grid or numerical labels are supplied.

answer.short:
A smooth U-shaped curve above the $x$-axis, with its minimum slightly to the right of the $y$-axis.

Add the two ordinates at each $x$.
answer.worked: On the far left, the exponential-shaped ordinate is close to zero, so the sum lies just above the decreasing line. On the right, the rising curve dominates. Add the ordinates between these regions to obtain a smooth positive minimum slightly to the right of the $y$-axis.

spec.description: Positive U-shaped sum with a minimum just right of the vertical axis and dashed input graphs.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative ordinate-addition sketch; no exact turning-point coordinates are asserted.

spec.description: An increasing blue line through the origin and a finite red wave with one positive crest and one negative trough.
spec.mathematics: The red curve begins at the origin and ends on the positive x-axis. Its finite domain bounds the sum.

answer.short:
The sum starts at the origin, rises to a crest, falls below the $x$-axis, then rises to a positive right endpoint on the line.

Add the wave's signed ordinates to the line.
answer.worked: Where the wave is positive, place the sum above the line; where it is negative, place it below the line. At the wave's three zeros, the sum meets the line. The negative trough is large enough to put part of the sum below the $x$-axis. Retain the wave's two finite endpoints.

spec.description: Finite sum with closed endpoints, a positive crest and a trough below the axis.
spec.mathematics: The sum path is obtained by adding the line's height to each control point of the supplied wave reconstruction.

spec.description: A blue upward-opening parabola with vertex at the origin and a red upper semicircle centred on the origin.
spec.mathematics: Symmetric unscaled curves. The sum exists only across the semicircle's finite domain.

answer.short:
A finite symmetric curve above the $x$-axis, with a central minimum and a small crest on each side. Its endpoints lie on the parabola.

Add ordinates only over the semicircle's domain.
answer.worked: Both ordinates are nonnegative, so the sum stays above the $x$-axis. At the centre, only the semicircle contributes. At its endpoints, only the parabola contributes. Add intermediate ordinates to obtain two small outer crests and a central minimum; retain the finite endpoints.

spec.description: Symmetric finite sum with closed elevated endpoints, two outer crests and a central dip.
spec.mathematics: Native ordinate sum of the normalized question-figure shapes; coordinates are not printed givens.

spec.description: A blue positive arch and a red wave share the origin and a finite positive x-axis endpoint.
spec.mathematics: The red wave has one positive crest, an interior zero and a negative trough. Neither curve has outward continuation arrows.

answer.short: The sum joins the shared endpoints on the $x$-axis, rises to a positive crest and then dips below the axis before returning to the right endpoint.
answer.worked: Both ordinates are positive in the left region, so the sum lies above both input graphs there. At the wave's interior zero, the sum lies on the blue arch. Farther right, the negative wave exceeds the positive arch in magnitude, giving a trough below the $x$-axis. Both endpoint sums are zero.

spec.description: Finite sum with a high positive crest, an interior axis crossing and a shallow negative trough.
spec.mathematics: The aligned Bézier component control ordinates are added to construct the sum.

spec.description: A blue increasing S-shaped graph through the origin approaches two dashed horizontal asymptotes. A positive symmetric red bell-shaped graph peaks above the upper asymptote.
spec.mathematics: The red ordinate approaches zero at both ends; the sum inherits the blue graph's two horizontal limiting levels.
spec.answerVisibility: Component graphs and supplied dashed asymptotes only.

answer.short:
The sum approaches the lower dashed asymptote on the left, crosses the $x$-axis left of the $y$-axis, reaches a crest near the $y$-axis and approaches the upper dashed asymptote from above on the right.

The bell's positive ordinates lift the S-shaped graph.
answer.worked: Add the positive bell ordinate to the S-shaped ordinate at each $x$. At the $y$-axis, the sum equals the bell's height because the S-shaped graph is zero there. The sum crosses the $x$-axis to the left and reaches a crest near the $y$-axis. At both far ends, the bell approaches zero, so the sum retains the two horizontal asymptotes.

spec.description: An asymmetric elevated crest with a negative left tail and positive right tail approaching the two supplied asymptotes.
spec.mathematics: The finite drawing window includes the crest and right-hand tail approaching the upper asymptote from above.

spec.description: A symmetric blue V has its vertex below the axis. A red upper semicircle ends at the V's two x-intercepts.
spec.mathematics: At the centre the input ordinates cancel. At the semicircle endpoints both ordinates are zero.

answer.short: Two symmetric positive humps meeting at the origin, with both outer endpoints on the $x$-axis.
answer.worked: At the centre, the semicircle's positive ordinate cancels the V's negative ordinate. Both endpoint sums are zero. Between these points, the semicircle's ordinate exceeds the magnitude of the negative V ordinate, giving two positive humps. Use only the semicircle's domain.

spec.description: Two symmetric positive humps with closed endpoints and a sharp meeting point at the origin.
spec.mathematics: Sum of the normalized V and semicircle over the finite common domain.

spec.description: A blue increasing concave-down curve starts at the origin. A red first-quadrant reciprocal-shaped curve approaches both positive axes.
spec.mathematics: The common domain is x>0; the reciprocal-shaped curve dominates near the vertical axis.

answer.short: For $x>0$, a positive curve with vertical asymptote $x=0$, one minimum and an increasing right tail approaching the blue curve from above.
answer.worked: Near the positive side of the $y$-axis, the red ordinate is large, so the sum tends upward without bound. Farther right, the red contribution decreases while the blue graph increases, giving a minimum. As the red ordinate approaches zero, the sum approaches the blue graph from above. There is no sum point at the origin.

spec.description: A positive sum descending from the vertical asymptote to a minimum, then rising above the increasing input graph.
spec.mathematics: Common domain x>0; no finite endpoint at the origin.

spec.description: Oppositely directed blue and red concave-down curves intersect on the positive y-axis. Their finite endpoints lie on opposite sides of the x-axis origin.
spec.mathematics: The sum exists only between the red curve's left endpoint and the blue curve's right endpoint.

answer.short: A finite symmetric arch above the $x$-axis, with a maximum on the $y$-axis and two positive endpoints.
answer.worked: Use only the interval where both curves are defined. At each interval endpoint, one ordinate is zero and the other is positive, so the sum endpoint lies above the $x$-axis. At the $y$-axis the equal positive ordinates add. Join the added ordinates in a symmetric concave-down arch.

spec.description: A symmetric concave-down answer arch with two closed positive endpoints and a central maximum.
spec.mathematics: Restricted common domain; each endpoint sum equals the other component's positive ordinate.

spec.description: A blue increasing logarithmic-shaped curve exists right of the y-axis. Red reciprocal-shaped branches lie in the first and third quadrants.
spec.mathematics: Only the positive reciprocal branch has a common domain with the blue curve. Both inputs approach the vertical axis.
spec.answerVisibility: Both supplied reciprocal branches and the blue input curve remain visible.

answer.short: For $x>0$, a positive curve tending upward near $x=0$, falling to one minimum and then rising toward the blue curve from above. There is no negative-$x$ branch.
answer.worked: Use only $x>0$, where both inputs exist. Near the vertical axis, the positive reciprocal-shaped ordinate dominates the negative blue ordinate, so the sum tends upward without bound. Add ordinates to locate a positive minimum. Farther right, the red contribution approaches zero and the sum approaches the blue curve from above.

spec.description: Only a positive-x answer branch, with a vertical asymptote, positive minimum and increasing right tail.
spec.mathematics: The negative red input branch is a dashed reference only; it does not generate a sum branch.

spec.description: A blue upward-opening parabola has vertex at the origin. Two positive red reciprocal-squared-shaped branches approach the y-axis and x-axis symmetrically.
spec.mathematics: The red graph is undefined on the vertical axis. The sum has symmetric left and right branches.

answer.short:
Two symmetric positive U-shaped branches, each with one minimum. Both tend upward beside $x=0$ and approach the parabola from above outward.

Add ordinates separately on either side of the vertical asymptote.
answer.worked: The sum is undefined at $x=0$. On either side, the red ordinate becomes large near the vertical axis, so both sum branches tend upward without bound. Moving outward, the red contribution decreases while the parabola rises, producing a positive minimum on each branch. The sum then approaches the parabola from above. Reflect one branch across the $y$-axis to obtain the other.

spec.description: Two symmetric positive U-shaped answer branches with a vertical asymptote at the y-axis and one minimum on each side.
spec.mathematics: Native sum of the normalized positive input shapes. No origin point or connection across the asymptote.
